Definition: from G3563; to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed:--consider, perceive, think, understand.
BiblicalUsage: To understand is to see what is plainly there, and Jesus and Paul both press it. Jesus asks His disciples whether they do not yet understand what goes into the mouth, and Paul says the invisible things of God are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, so that men are without excuse.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that understanding is a duty, not a gift for the few: creation itself teaches the power and Godhead of God, and no one can plead that he did not see.
